To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hypertension is associated with endothelial dysfunction and low grade inflammation, and that the latter contributes to the pathophysiological mechanisms of hypertension.

(i) the endothelium plays an important role in the development of hypertension; (ii) endothelial dysfunction in hypertension is associated with increased vascular inflammation and increased oxidative stress; (iii) increased oxidative stress and inflammation in hypertension are related to the development of endothelial dysfunction and vascular remodeling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms involved in the development of hypertension and the role of the inflammatory response of endothelial cells in the pathogenesis of hypertension.
the study of the mechanisms involved in the development and progression of vascular dysfunction and atherosclerosis in experimental hypertension.
the study of the mechanisms involved in the pathophysiology and treatment of hypertension and its complications, with the aim of developing new strategies for the management of these patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hypertension, a common disease, is a multifactorial disorder that results from the interaction between genetic and environmental factors.
hypertension and vascular dysfunction are closely linked and that endothelial dysfunction is an early and important step in the development of vascular complications in hypertension.
endothelial dysfunction is an important contributor to hypertension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we demonstrated a role for the endothelium in the regulation of blood pressure, and that endothelial dysfunction is a key feature in the development and progression of experimental hypertension.
we have identified a new mechanism by which hypertension causes endothelial dysfunction.
we demonstrated the role of vascular inflammation in the pathogenesis of hypertension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the endothelium plays an important role in the pathogenesis of hypertension, as it is a major determinant of vascular tone and a regulator of vascular inflammation and thrombogenesis.

the endothelium plays a central role in the development of hypertension and its complications, and that endothelial dysfunction is a common denominator in the pathophysiology and complications of hypertension.
the endothelium is the main player in the regulation of vascular tone, and its dysfunction contributes to the pathogenesis of hypertension and cardiovascular disease.
